A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SRUM and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite reformatting, renumbering, and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SRUM experiments on Bagel and BLIP3o, including benchmark evaluations, reward ablations, activation analyses, and generalization tests.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds traditional-metric results, reward-model comparisons, timing measurements, and failure-case evaluations.

M1.justification: The candidate-generation pipeline, global/local rewards, and training objective in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. v2 explicitly documents frozen, offline reward scoring and cached rewards without establishing a procedural revision. SAM grounding for Bagel and native grounding for BLIP3o were already documented in v1 Appendix A.

E1.justification: The training and benchmark datasets remain unchanged. New Appendix D adds limited qualitative scenarios involving arithmetic-to-fruit mapping, before/after Industrial Revolution imagery, and aesthetic chair generation, extending the tested requirements without adding a benchmark suite.

E2.justification: New Table 3 evaluates ReCA, UnifiedReward, and external Qwen2.5-VL 7B/32B reward models against SRUM; v1 only discussed ReCA and used Qwen models as evaluators. Table 2 additionally evaluates Show-o, distinct from the retained Show-O2 comparator, and Appendix D adds a qualitative nano-banana comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds traditional T2I-CompBench evaluation metrics alongside Qwen-based scoring, external-scorer configurations with and without global rewards, and a timing evaluation involving 6K candidate images. Existing benchmark protocols, non-CoT ReasonBench evaluation, and the appendix training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds local-reward removal results, scorer calibration and accept/reject analysis, and computational-efficiency comparisons. Appendix D introduces three illustrated failure studies. Earlier ablation and activation plots are retained; the new local-reward drops are reported in prose, not added to Figure 3.

E5.justification: v2 introduces a correlation-based calibration diagnostic on saved image/prompt pairs, reporting rho values of 0.58 versus 0.43. This is a limited addition to statistical reporting: neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the new correlation estimator is not specified.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the four retained benchmark tables match. v2 adds traditional-metric results and Table 3 comparisons, including UnifiedReward 85.15, ReCA 86.45, and Qwen-32B with global reward 88.01 versus SRUM 88.37. New ablation, calibration, timing, and qualitative failure outcomes substantially expand the results rather than improve previously reported same-setting scores.

T1.justification: Appendix B, Algorithm 1 newly defines functional clusters through percentile thresholding of maximum mean FFN activations and assignment by task preference; v1 assumed precomputed clusters. This adds a mathematical cluster definition. The loss equations and activation-average formulas remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the central claims of self-rewarding UMM post-training, dual global/local feedback, and strong compositional and reasoning generalization. The headline scores remain 82.18 to 88.37 and 43.82 to 46.75. Added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes differences between traditional and Qwen-based evaluation to logical-parsing limitations, and interprets internal-scorer calibration as explaining its advantage over larger external scorers. Appendix D adds boundaries involving understanding errors, insufficient causal training data, and aesthetics. These substantially extend the earlier mechanism discussion and prompting/scaling limitations.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents frozen reward generation, cached offline rewards, generation/flow updates, cluster-construction pseudocode, and scoring hardware and computational costs. Conversely, v1 Table 7's complete local-reward prompt becomes an abbreviated template with ellipses and fewer examples in v2 Table 9. The training hyperparameter table and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to SILMM, CLIP, and Detecting Everything in the Open World, refines the architecture taxonomy, and sharpens positioning against external-reward approaches. Most cited literature and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged; the conversion to numbered references is formatting.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and narrative remain intact. v2 tightens abstract and method prose, rewrites parts of the architecture and activation explanations, replaces 'KL constraint' with 'reference constraint' in the discussion, and updates affiliations and acknowledgements. New empirical subheadings and Appendix D extend the existing organization.

P2.justification: A document-wide template change alters typography, text area, running headers, table sizing, and figure placement. v2 adds two results tables and a failure-image gallery, and expands Algorithm 1 into a full-page, two-column display. The content of Figures 1–6 is retained despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through traditional metrics, relevant post-training and reward-model comparisons, and additional ablation and failure evidence. It also clarifies offline training and cluster construction. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new calibration/comparison procedures and the loss of the complete local-reward prompt. The added evidence and clarity provide a modest net improvement.
